start_dose_credit.formula: implied_credit = c0 + (1 - c0) * f, f = (low_daily_mg - label_start_mg) / (anchor_mg - label_start_mg); value = mean of the four c0
start_dose_credit.basis: estimated from two randomized dose comparisons (ATLAS for lisinopril, HEAAL for losartan) with large uncertainty; carried to every other class
start_dose_credit.audit_note: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E11): the value 0.364 recomputes (0.36425). It uses proxy anchors for the full-credit dose (16.79 and 110.43 mg) while the trials' own high arms were 33.2 mg (ATLAS) and 129 mg (HEAAL); re-solved with those the four credits are 0.6, 0.269, 0.394, 0.365, mean 0.407 (about 41% rather than 36%). The hazard-ratio inputs mix Flather Peto odds ratios with ATLAS Cox hazard ratios. The stated range [0.206, 0.565] is the spread of four points, not an interval: the HEAAL death credit runs from -0.364 to 1.307 across the interval of its hazard ratio (0.84-1.04) and the HEAAL hospitalization credit from 0.00 to 0.93, so the credit from HEAAL alone is not bounded. "Measured for ACE inhibitors and ARBs" overstated it. The value is unchanged; it is an engine estimate.

source.citation: Vardeny O et al. Eur J Heart Fail 2016;18:1228-34 (PMC5095784)

anchors.quote: The majority of patients remained on target doses after randomization, with final mean achieved doses of 375 mg daily and 18.9 mg daily respectively.
anchors.arithmetic: 375 / 400 = 0.9375. Daily dose counted as sacubitril + valsartan total (97/103 bid = 400).
anchors.notes: All patients tolerated target-dose sacubitril/valsartan in the active run-in before randomization, so 375 mg describes a pre-selected population; it says nothing about de novo starts. Row RR is an indirect (putative-placebo) estimate. 42% had a dose reduction at some point (Vardeny abstract).

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: SOLVD-T (Kondo Table 1): 'Enalapril (1285) ... 20 mg | 16.6 mg (E) 18.0 mg (P)'; SOLVD-P: '16.9 mg (E) e 18.2 mg (P) e'
anchors.arithmetic: D2: fraction 0.839 = (1285 x 16.6/20 + 2111 x 16.9/20) / (1285 + 2111) = (1066.6 + 1783.8)/3396 (SOLVD-T and SOLVD-P enalapril arms; protocol target 20 mg/day); x lowest flagged formulary target 20 mg/day = 16.79 mg/day.
anchors.notes: Lisinopril target is flagged at 20, 30 and 40 mg; the lowest (20) is the denominator as the engine's first-flagged target. No placebo-controlled lisinopril trial exists. ATLAS used 32.5-35 mg as the high arm. Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E11): SOLVD-P (2,111 of the 3,396 patients, 62% of the weighting) enrolled asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction without overt heart failure, and its footnote reads "Doses/proportions shown were obtained from prescription at the last visit. By the end of the trial, 24% had discontinued enalapril." The earlier note disclosed the discontinuation for SOLVD-T only.
anchors.dose_population: Enalapril arms of SOLVD-T and SOLVD-P, among patients still on drug at the last visit (not all randomized patients)

The trial RR is an intention-to-treat estimate, so it reflects the diluted 11.2 mg average exposure; the on-drug dose is 16.6. Judgement: anchor kept at the on-drug dose (a patient modelled as taking the drug), flagged for the controller. SAVE, AIRE and TRACE patients (73% of the pooled 12,763) have no verified dose. By the end of the trial, 24% had discontinued enalapril." The earlier note disclosed the discontinuation for SOLVD-T only.

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: COPERNICUS | Carvedilol (1156) Placebo (1133) | ... | 50 mg | 37 mg (C) e 41 mg (P) e | 65% (C) e 78% (P) e | Kondo Table 2 footnote: "daily dose in surviving patients at 120 days (65% 50 mg, 11% 25 mg, 9% 12.5 mg, 6% 6.25 mg, 9% 0 mg)"
anchors.notes: Single secondary source. The carvedilol label confirms the COPERNICUS dose ceiling (up to 50 mg/day) but gives no mean (its 42 mg/day figure is COMET, its 20 mg bid figure is CAPRICORN). The trial target was 25 mg bid for all; the formulary target is 100 mg/day above 85 kg dry weight, where 37 mg is 0.37 of the formulary target. The beta-blocker HFH row rests on CIBIS-II alone, not COPERNICUS. Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E11): the 37 mg is a day-120 mean among SURVIVORS and it includes 9% at zero; it recomputes from the footnote (0.65 x 50 + 0.11 x 25 + 0.09 x 12.5 + 0.06 x 6.25 + 0.09 x 0 = 36.75 mg). Among those still taking the drug the mean would be about 40 mg (36.75 / 0.91).
anchors.dose_population: Mean among COPERNICUS patients still alive at day 120, including the 9% who were taking no drug (zero)

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: CIBIS II | Bisoprolol (1327) Placebo (1320) | ... | 10 mg | 6.2 mg (B) 7.3 mg (P) (Kondo)  versus Tillman: 'CIBIS-II 10 Bisoprolol (8.6 mg daily) versus placebo'
anchors.arithmetic: D3 -> D2: fraction 0.775 = (1990 x 159/200 + 1156 x 37/50)/(1990+1156) = (1582.05 + 855.44)/3146; x 10 mg = 7.75 mg/day. Both CIBIS-II figures recorded: 6.2 mg (0.62) and 8.6 mg (0.86); the proxy sits between them.
anchors.notes: CIBIS-II is excluded from the pooled fraction because its mean cannot be settled from a primary source. Tillman's CIBIS-II row also says 'No significant difference in all-cause death', which contradicts the trial abstract (HR 0.66, p<0.0001), so that row is unreliable. Distribution facts read from a review citing the Lancet paper: 564 (42.5%) on 10 mg, 152 on 7.5, 176 on 5 in the maintenance phase; Simon 2003: 434 on 1.25-3.75 mg. Computed from those counts, the mean of the 892 patients on 5 mg or more is 8.59 mg (matches 8.6), and the mean of all 1,327 would be 6.2-7.0 mg depending on the low-dose split (matches the low end near 6.2). So 8.6 may be a mean among patients on 5 mg or more and 6.2 a mean that counts the low-dose group, but this is inference, not a settled fact.

source.citation: Aldactone label (DailyMed set id 0fed2822-3a03-4b64-9857-c682fcd462bc), section 14; Pitt B et al. NEJM 1999;341:709-17

anchors.quote: The mean daily dose at study end for patients randomized to spironolactone was 26 mg. (Kondo Table 3: 26 mg (S); Tillman: 'Spironolactone (26 mg daily)')
anchors.arithmetic: D1: 26 / 50 = 0.52. The formulary target is 25 mg when eGFR <50 (fraction 1.04 there).
anchors.notes: Only 12% reached 50 mg (Kondo). RALES median CrCl 57 mL/min. The trial effect is the effect of about 26 mg; nothing below 25 mg was measured. Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E11): the Aldactone label gives the mean "for patients randomized to spironolactone" and Kondo Table 3 footnote c says "among patients continuing to receive treatment after 24 months"; the denominators conflict (all randomized patients against those still on drug at 24 months) and neither was disclosed in the row before.
anchors.dose_population: Two denominators that disagree: the label says patients randomized to spironolactone (mean at study end 26 mg); Kondo Table 3 footnote c says patients continuing to receive treatment after 24 months

source.citation: Swedberg K et al. Lancet 2010;376:875-85, via Tillman 2019 (PMC6535737) and Cardiology Trials review

anchors.quote: Tillman: 'SHIFT Ivabradine (6.5 mg twice daily) versus placebo'. Review: 'The mean ivabradine dose was 6.4 mg twice a day at 4 weeks and 6.5mg twice a day at 1 year.'
anchors.arithmetic: D1: 6.5 mg bid = 13 mg/day. Fraction 13/10 = 1.30 of the lowest flagged target (5 bid = 10/day); 13/15 = 0.867 of the highest (7.5 bid). Inside the formulary range (10 or 5 to 15), so D5 does not bind.
anchors.notes: Two secondary sources, no primary text. Corlanor label: benefit appeared to decrease as the beta-blocker dose increased, little if any benefit at guideline target doses of beta-blockers.

source.citation: Digitalis Investigation Group. NEJM 1997;336:525-33; van Veldhuisen DJ et al. Nat Med 2026;32:2647-53 (PMC13375525)

anchors.quote: DIG abstract: 'median dose of digoxin, 0.25 mg per day'. DECISION: 'As defined by the algorithm, 75% of patients started the study with 0.1 mg digoxin once daily and 25% of patients with 0.2 mg once daily.'
anchors.arithmetic: DIG median 0.25 mg/day exceeds the formulary's highest strength (0.125 mg = 125 mcg); D5 clamps to 0.125 mg/day. DECISION start mean (0.75 x 0.1 + 0.25 x 0.2) = 0.125 mg/day (computed; titrated to serum level 0.5-0.9 ng/mL afterwards, mean achieved dose not reported). Both land at 0.125.
anchors.notes: Formulary has no flagged target, so the fraction is stated against the highest strength (1.0). DIG reported a median, not a mean. The researcher's alternative '0.0625-0.125 mg' for DECISION is not in the primary text. Unit in the formulary is mcg (125 mcg).
anchors.unit_correction: 2026-11-16: the anchor was stored as 0.125 mg/day (research unit) but the formulary doses digoxin in mcg (62.5 and 125), so every dose compared as above the anchor. Stored now in the formulary unit: 125 mcg/day (= 0.125 mg/day). Provenance fields unchanged.
